brandVoice.summary: Approachable authority. Warm, practical, classic. Never stiff, never trendy, never corporate jargon.
writingStyle: Short, punchy sentences for headlines and social
Longer, confident prose for product descriptions
Lead with the customer's reality — not the product name
Use real scenarios: meetings, commutes, events
Soft CTAs — 'shop the look', not 'buy now'

targetCustomer.name: The Polished Professional
targetCustomer.description: She wants to look polished and credible at work without overthinking it. She values versatility, quality, and fair price.
targetCustomer.quote: I don't want to think about what I'm wearing — I want to think about the meeting I'm walking into.

dos: Use refined, elegant, and practical language
Write 1 paragraph + 4–6 bullet points for product descriptions
Start bullet points with an active verb (Features, Crafted, Designed, Finished)
Reference fabric, fit, key details, and versatility in bullets
Keep copy SEO-optimized — include occasion, silhouette, fabric keywords
Reference real-life occasions: boardroom, weekend brunch, client dinner
Write as a peer talking to an accomplished woman — not a salesperson
donts: Do NOT refer to the woman wearing the product ('she', 'her', 'the wearer')
Do NOT repeat the style name in the opening paragraph
Do NOT use 'girlboss', 'slay', 'boss babe' or similar slang
Do NOT use corporate jargon or overly formal language
Do NOT describe as 'cheap', 'affordable', 'budget' — use 'accessible' or 'exceptional value'
Do NOT use aspirational fantasy — keep it real and grounded

productDescription.paragraphGuidance: Describe the piece using refined, practical language. Highlight the occasion, the feeling, and the versatility. Do NOT start with the product name. ~2–3 sentences.
productDescription.bulletGuidance: Each bullet = one key feature. Start with an active verb. Cover: fabric/material, silhouette/fit, key design detail, versatility/occasion.

example.title: Bedford Stretch Blazer
example.paragraph: A refined take on the tailored blazer, cut from stretch fabric that moves with you through a full day. Clean lines and a polished silhouette make it equally at home in the boardroom or at dinner.
bullets: Crafted from stretch fabric for all-day comfort
Single-button closure for a clean front
Front welt pockets for a structured finish
Pairs effortlessly with trousers or dress pants

emailSubjectLine.guidance: Lead with the offer or the occasion — not the brand name. Use tension or specificity. Avoid clickbait.
examples: Offer-forward: '15% Off Your First Order — Inside'
Editorial: 'The Spring Work Wardrobe Edit Is Here'

emailPreviewText.guidance: Treat preview text as a second subject line — add information, don't repeat the subject.
examples: Shop our Spring workwear edit — offer expires in 48 hours.
Timeless workwear for the woman who's earned her confidence.
New arrivals: blazers, trousers, and dresses built for the workweek.

instagramCaption.structure: 1–2 punchy opening lines + context sentence + hashtags
instagramCaption.guidance: Open with a real scenario or sharp observation. Grounded, not aspirational fantasy. Soft CTA. End with 5–8 hashtags.
instagramCaption.example:
The meeting ran long. The blazer didn't flinch.

Shop the Bedford Stretch Blazer — link in bio.

#AnneKlein #WorkwearStyle #WomenWhoWork #ProfessionalWomen #TailoredStyle

heroHeadline.guidance: Headline speaks to the customer's reality. Subhead adds context and grounds it in product/benefit.

examples.headline: Dressed. Done. Ready for Whatever.
examples.subhead: Anne Klein clothing, shoes, and bags built for the workweek — so getting ready stops being a decision.

examples.headline: The Work Wardrobe That Works.
examples.subhead: Versatile, polished, and built to last — because you have better things to think about.

dresses.title: V-Neck Midi Dress
dresses.paragraph: A sleeveless midi silhouette with soft draping that carries through a full workday without losing its shape. Refined enough for a client presentation; versatile enough for an evening out.
bullets: Sleeveless A-line silhouette with flattering V-neckline
Midi length with soft draping fabric
Zipper closure at back for a clean finish
Transitions seamlessly from office to evening

blazers.title: Bedford Stretch Blazer
blazers.paragraph: Cut from stretch fabric for a tailored fit that moves with you. Clean notched lapels and a single-button closure keep the silhouette sharp without being stiff.
bullets: Crafted from stretch fabric for all-day comfort
Single-button closure for a clean front
Front welt pockets with structured finish
Pairs with trousers, dresses, or denim

tops.title: Sleeveless Shell
tops.paragraph: A clean, lightweight knit with an uncluttered neckline — the kind of piece that goes under a blazer on Monday and stands alone on Friday.
bullets: Tucks cleanly into trousers or skirts
Versatile base layer for workwear dressing
